description: Just trying to build a great product.
summary: SPHEREx Explorer is an interactive, browser-based astronomical workspace developed to explore sky images and spectrophotometric data from NASA's SPHEREx mission across 102 infrared bands (0.75–5.0 μm) and 6 detector arrays. Traditional infrared astronomy requires downloading massive FITS files and writing custom analysis scripts. Our solution addresses the challenge by streaming calibrated cutouts directly from the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) into a zero-install web application. Users can search any celestial coordinates, animate multi-epoch blink comparisons, execute client-side difference imaging, plot 102-band spectral energy distributions (SEDs), decode pixel bitmask flags, and overlay catalogs from NASA WISE, ESA Gaia DR3, and CSA NEOSSat. SPHEREx Explorer accelerates scientific triage for researchers while making infrared astrophysics accessible to students and citizen scientists worldwide.
details:
WHAT DOES IT DO & HOW DOES IT WORK?

SPHEREx Explorer is a full-stack web workspace designed to visualize, compare, and analyze sky cutouts and spectral data from NASA's SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer) mission. Instead of requiring users to manually download gigabytes of archival FITS files and run local Python scripts, SPHEREx Explorer automates the entire scientific pipeline in the browser:

1. Precision Coordinate Search & URL State Synchronization:

Users can query any celestial coordinates (RA/Dec) in decimal degrees or sexagesimal (HMS/DMS) formats. Every workspace parameter—coordinates, active detector arrays, spectral channels, and stretch settings—synchronizes with URL query parameters for one-click sharing of scientific findings.

2. 102 Infrared Bands & 6 Detector Arrays (Dual UI Modes):

Mirroring SPHEREx's Linear Variable Filter (LVF) optics, our tool organizes observations across 6 detector arrays and 102 spectral channels (0.75–5.0 μm). Users can switch between "Simple Mode" (array-level navigation for students) and "Advanced Mode" (granular 102-channel selection for researchers).

3. Multi-Epoch Blink Comparator & Split-Screen Slider:

An interactive Blink Viewport with adjustable cadence and an A/B Compare Slider allow instant detection of:

• High Proper Motion Stars: Tracking rapid positional shifts across epochs (e.g., Barnard's Star).

• Ultra-Cool Brown Dwarfs: Highlighting cold objects like WISE 0855 (08h55m10.831s, -7d14m42.53s) and Epsilon Indi B, which are invisible at shorter wavelengths due to methane/water absorption but glow brightly in mid-infrared bands (~3.8–4.8 μm).

• Variable Stars: Observing flux variations in targets like RW Aurigae and R Draconis.

4. Client-Side Web Worker Image Math & Dynamic Stretching:

A dedicated browser Web Worker computes real-time difference images (Frame A minus Frame B) to isolate moving objects or transients without blocking the UI thread, supporting Linear, Logarithmic, Asinh, and Percentile dynamic range stretching.

5. Spectrophotometry (SED Plotter) & Bitmask Quality Inspector:

An interactive Spectrum Plotter graphs the target's Spectral Energy Distribution (SED) across all 102 channels, while the Metadata Inspector decodes pixel-level bitmask flags (saturation, cosmic rays, ghosting, persistence, bad pixels) and World Coordinate System (WCS) headers.

6. Multi-Mission Catalog Overlays & Mover Candidates:

The viewport cross-matches the sky field in real time against NASA WISE (infrared photometry), ESA Gaia DR3 (optical astrometry and proper motion vectors), and CSA NEOSSat (near-Earth object detections), flagging moving object candidates.

SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE

• Backend Engine: Python, FastAPI, and Astropy query the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) via Simple Image Access (SIA) and Table Access Protocol (TAP), performing WCS tangent-plane reprojection, FITS cutout generation, spectral extraction, and multi-tier caching.

• Frontend Client: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS render multi-layer HTML5 canvases, run Web Worker array math, and display an interactive custom Blender 3D model (.glb) of the SPHEREx spacecraft via Three.js/WebGL.

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

• Rapid Scientific Triage: Compresses hours of FITS data reduction and catalog cross-matching into a two-second browser query.

• Educational & Global Accessibility: Bridges professional astrophysics and public outreach through pre-configured benchmark targets, integrated documentation, and full bilingual (English/Ukrainian) localization.

HOW IS OUR PROJECT CREATIVE & WHAT FACTORS DID WE CONSIDER?

• Creative Synthesis: We unified three traditionally separate workflows—time-domain blinking, pixel subtraction math, and 102-channel spectrophotometry—into a single synchronized screen accompanied by an interactive 3D spacecraft model.

• Scientific Rigor & Usability Factors: Our team considered real-world observational challenges, such as distinguishing true astrophysical transients from instrumental artifacts (solved via bitmask flag overlays), handling vastly different flux scales across 0.75–5.0 μm (solved via Asinh/Log stretching), and ensuring smooth performance on standard laptops (solved via Web Workers and backend caching).

TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED

• Languages: Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3

• Backend & Science: FastAPI, Astropy, NumPy, SciPy, Uvicorn

• Frontend & 3D: React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Web Workers API, Three.js / WebGL, Blender

• Infrastructure & Repo: Cloudflare Tunnel & Edge Caching, Git/GitHub (https://github.com/xto-ia/SPHEREx-explorer)

SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) DISCLOSURE In accordance with NASA Space Apps Challenge guidelines, we transparently disclose that the entire codebase, project logo, and 3D spacecraft model of SPHEREx Explorer were AI-generated using the OpenCode agent harness (powered by the DeepSeek v4.1 Flash model) via Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations. Additionally, Google Gemini (Hydrogen and Argon) was utilized for technical consultations, architectural guidance, astronomical domain research, and documentation/translation support. All project ideation, system requirements, prompt engineering, testing, and scientific verification were directed and validated by Larping Team.
